issue.title: build: output consistency and speed improvements

repository.name: clarity
repository.description: Clarity is a scalable, accessible, customizable, open source design system built with web components. Works with any JavaScript framework, built for enterprises, and designed to  be inclusive.

issue.body:
## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->

* [ ] Bugfix
* [ ] Feature
* [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
* [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
* [x] Build related changes
* [x] CI related changes
* [ ] Documentation content changes
* [ ] clarity.design website / infrastructure changes
* [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the new behavior?

This PR has two primary changes:

**First**: ensure that all our apps, `website`, `dev` and `dev-core` all use the proper library build output that the Angular CLI generates. This ensures that what we are testing/using in our apps is exactly what our users would consume through NPM. This may become the necessary default for the watch step depending on the Angular 9 update for mono repos. https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/33659 

**Second**: improve parallelization across the build as well as the Angular unit tests.
This change improves the Angular unit test execution time by **30-40%** and overall build execution time by **15%**.

By splitting the tests across two cores it improves the test execution speed. Two cores is important as if you ramp up to many threads the overhead of starting up that many Chrome instances cancels out any benefits of running on multiple threads. This improvement also includes adding the `website` project as part of the final build to ensure output consistency.

Contributors to the project should be able simply run `npm run build` and consistently build the entire project minus the visual diff tests. This includes making sure all libraries, test apps and website will run properly with the latest changes.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

* [ ] Yes
* [x] No
